answer: An agent marketplace requires each trading identity to lock a refundable bond for 30 days before it can bid, with one active bid per bond. Agents named lotus, ember, and relic face the same rule: creating more names creates no extra bidding capacity unless each name posts its own bond. An attacker running 1,000 identities must therefore immobilize 1,000 bonds, paying the financing cost of that capital for the full lock period.
